text: Imagine the ground under your feet stopping for exactly one second. At the equator you are already moving east at about 465 meters per second. The road stops, but your body keeps going. In that single second you move nearly 465 meters relative to the ground, about four football fields, without taking a step. Gravity still holds you down, the danger is sideways, the air, clouds, and ocean keep their momentum too. When the ground starts again, land, air, water, and everything loose are no longer aligned. That mismatch is the real disaster. What moves first? You, the atmosphere, or the ocean?
